items.title: 61124_Mario Bauza oral history interview
items.q: I would call a modern version of Paul Whiteman with more excitement

ctx.x: And they don't sound like this and don't sound like that. And then the American musicians, they got a conception about Cuban music, (inaudible), that's what they think about. (Inaudible). But they were completely wrong. So I went a

couple of times to their rehearsal, and, you know, they all liked me and (inaudible) but with that band (inaudible) good piano, Afro-Cuban. Let's face it, because the jazz band never was good, because the band was too clumsy. There was not a player, as you say, I would call a modern version of Paul Whiteman with more excitement (inaudible). They went for a climax and harmony, you know what I mean, dynamics this different (inaudible). You could call that dance -- but nobody could dance by that band. There was no…

So he tried the other rhythm, and the other rhythm (inaudible). Up to today that (inaudible) never, never, never could swing (inaudible) band for kids (inaudible) or the brass AND THAT WAS THAT. (inaudible).
